info.title: bowire
info.description: Bowire — standalone CLI + browser UI for the multi-protocol API workbench. Discover, invoke, record, mock, and replay across gRPC, REST, GraphQL, MQTT, SignalR, WebSocket, SSE, MCP, OData, and Socket.IO — every first-party plugin pre-bundled. Run `bowire --url …` for the browser UI or `bowire list/describe/call` / `bowire mock` for grpcurl-style scripting and recording replay.

x-inspectra.cliParsedDescription: Bowire — multi-protocol API workbench. Run without a subcommand to launch the browser UI; run a subcommand (discover / list / describe / call / catalogue / mock / mcp / plugin / test) for scripting.

options.name: --no-browser
options.description: Don't auto-open a browser window. [default: False]

options.name: --enable-mcp-adapter
options.description: Expose discovered services as MCP tools. [default: False]

options.name: --auto-create-initial-workspace
options.description: Seed a default "Personal" workspace on first run instead of the empty Home + Create-Workspace CTA. Standalone leaves this off by default so the operator meets the workspace concept up front; embedded hosts seed one automatically. Equivalent to Bowire:AutoCreateInitialWorkspace=true. [default: False]

options.name: --update-check
options.description: Opt in to the daily plugin-update check (off by default). Bowire queries nuget.org once per day for newer versions of every installed sibling plugin and surfaces a count badge in the sidebar. Equivalent to Bowire:PluginUpdateCheck:Enabled=true. [default: False]

options.name: --auth-provider
options.description: Id of the IBowireAuthProvider plugin that should gate workbench access (e.g. 'oidc'). When unset, the workbench stays open — same as today's laptop default. When set, the named plugin must be installed (e.g. `bowire plugin install Kuestenlogik.Bowire.Auth.Oidc`) or Bowire fails fast. Provider-namespaced flags are read from Bowire:Auth:<id>:* — for OIDC: --auth-oidc-authority, --auth-oidc-client-id, etc. (forwarded as Bowire:Auth:Oidc:Authority / ClientId).

options.name: --lock-server-url
options.description: Disable URL editing in the UI. [default: False]

options.name: --telemetry
options.description: Enable OpenTelemetry self-observability (#29). Bowire emits traces + Bowire-domain metrics (bowire.invoke.count / duration / bowire.discover.count / bowire.plugin.load / bowire.mock.requests) through the canonical 'Kuestenlogik.Bowire' Meter and ActivitySource. Wire endpoint, headers, and protocol come from the standard OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_* env vars. Off by default — laptop installs stay quiet. [default: False]

options.name: --telemetry-strip-method-labels
options.description: When --telemetry is on, drop the high-cardinality service + method dimensions from emitted metrics. Shared multi-tenant installs (GDPR / HIPAA / SOX) almost always want this; private-network deploys usually leave it off so per-method breakdowns survive. [default: False]

options.name: --ai-provider
options.description: AI provider id for the workbench's chat / hint surface (#25 Phase 2). Default 'ollama' speaks the local Ollama HTTP API on 127.0.0.1:11434; LM Studio on :1234 works through the same client because the wire shape matches. Cloud connectors slot in via the same Microsoft.Extensions.AI IChatClient seam in Phase 3. Maps to Bowire:Ai:ProviderId.

options.name: --ai-endpoint
options.description: Override the AI provider's HTTP endpoint. Default 'http://localhost:11434' (Ollama). Set to 'http://localhost:1234' for LM Studio, or to a remote Ollama gateway when the model server runs on another host. Maps to Bowire:Ai:Endpoint.

options.name: --ai-model
options.description: Model name passed to the AI provider. Default 'llama3.2:3b' (Ollama's small + free model that runs on a laptop). Use `ollama pull <name>` first; LM Studio uses whatever model is currently loaded. Maps to Bowire:Ai:Model.

options.name: --oast-server
options.description: Interaction-server URL for the Security rail's manual OAST panel (#486) — e.g. https://oast.example.com. Enables generating out-of-band callback payloads and watching the live feed, the interactive counterpart to `bowire scan --oast-server`. Point it at your own `bowire oast serve` instance. Maps to Bowire:Oast:Server.

options.name: --oast-token
options.description: Auth token for a gated interaction server (one started with `bowire oast serve --token`). Maps to Bowire:Oast:Token.

options.name: --catalogue-provider
options.description: Catalogue provider to read the URL catalogue from: 'local' (a JSON file), 'http' (a remote catalogue document), 'consul', 'kubernetes', or 'agent'. local / http / consul ship in the box; 'kubernetes' needs `bowire plugin install Kuestenlogik.Bowire.Catalogue.Kubernetes` and 'agent' needs `bowire plugin install Kuestenlogik.Bowire.Catalogue.Agent`. Maps to Bowire:Discovery:Catalogue:Provider.

options.name: --catalogue-path
options.description: Path to the catalogue JSON document read by the 'local' provider. Defaults to ~/.bowire/catalogue.json. Implies --catalogue-provider local when that flag is absent. Maps to Bowire:Discovery:Catalogue:Local:Path.

options.name: --catalogue-url
options.description: URL the 'http' catalogue provider GETs every refresh interval. Must return the catalogue document shape ({ "version": 1, "entries": [...] }). Implies --catalogue-provider http when that flag is absent. Maps to Bowire:Discovery:Catalogue:Http:Url.

options.name: --catalogue-consul
options.description: Consul agent address for the 'consul' catalogue provider (e.g. http://localhost:8500). Implies --catalogue-provider consul when that flag is absent. Maps to Bowire:Discovery:Catalogue:Consul:Address.

options.name: --plugin-dir
options.description: Override the plugin directory.

options.name: --map-basemap
options.description: Map widget basemap: 'osm' / 'satellite' / 'demotiles' / 'none', a tile URL with {z}/{x}/{y}, or a style.json URL. Default: 'demotiles'.

options.name: --disable-plugin
options.description: Skip a protocol plugin at startup. Repeat or comma-separate ('--disable-plugin grpc --disable-plugin signalr' or '--disable-plugin grpc,signalr'). Useful when a plugin DLL won't load or its discovery probe is too slow for the current host.

options.name: --disable-cli-command
options.description: Skip an auto-discovered CLI subcommand at startup. Mirrors --disable-plugin but for IBowireCliCommand contributions (scan / future plugin commands). Repeat or comma-separate.

commands.name: call
commands.description: Invoke a method on any loaded protocol plugin (grpcurl-style). Pin the plugin with `--protocol` or the `protocol@url` form; add `--stream` to follow a server-streaming, SSE, WebSocket or broker subscription.

options.name: --url
options.description: Target server URL. Accepts the `protocol@url` hint form (e.g. `grpc@https://localhost:5001`, `mqtt@tcp://broker:1883`) to pin one plugin and skip probing the rest. [default: https://localhost:5001]

options.name: -plaintext
options.description: Use plaintext (no TLS). [default: False]

options.name: -v
options.description: Verbose output (list). [default: False]

options.name: --compact
options.description: One-line JSON output (call, pipe-friendly). [default: False]

options.name: -d
options.description: JSON body (or @filename). Repeatable for client-streaming.

options.name: -H
options.description: Metadata header "key: value". Repeatable.

options.name: --protocol
options.description: Protocol plugin id to invoke through (grpc / rest / graphql / mqtt / …). Overrides a `protocol@url` prefix on --url. Without either, gRPC is assumed unless --stream is set, in which case every loaded plugin is probed and the one that owns the service wins.

options.name: --stream
options.description: Consume the method as a stream: prints one JSON document per received frame until the server ends the stream or you press Ctrl+C. gRPC server-streaming methods are detected automatically and don't need the flag. [default: False]

options.name: --var
options.description: Variable for the {{name}} / ${name} resolver that runs over -d, -H and --url. KEY=VALUE; repeatable. --env is an alias, matching `bowire test`.

options.name: --env-file
options.description: File with one KEY=VALUE per line (dotenv-style; blank lines and # comments ignored) for the resolver. Repeatable; --var repeats win over file entries.

commands.name: mock
commands.description: Replay a recording (or schema) as a local API endpoint. Pass a .bwr file as the positional argument for the common case, or use --schema / --grpc-schema / --graphql-schema for schema-only mocks.

options.name: --recording
options.description: Path to a Bowire recording JSON.

options.name: --schema
options.description: Path to an OpenAPI 3 document for schema-only mocks.

options.name: --grpc-schema
options.description: Path to a protobuf FileDescriptorSet (.pb).

options.name: --graphql-schema
options.description: Path to a GraphQL SDL file.

options.name: --port
options.description: Listen port. Default 6000. [default: 6000]

options.name: --host
options.description: Listen host. Default 127.0.0.1. [default: 127.0.0.1]

options.name: --https
options.description: Serve over HTTPS (self-signed localhost cert by default; supply --cert for your own). [default: False]

options.name: --https-port
options.description: Port for the HTTPS listener. Defaults to --port.

options.name: --cert
options.description: Path to a certificate for --https: a .pfx/.p12 (with --cert-password) or a PEM file.

options.name: --cert-password
options.description: Password for a PKCS#12 (.pfx/.p12) --cert.

options.name: --proxy
options.description: Forward unmatched requests to this upstream base URL (partial mocking). e.g. https://api.example.com.

options.name: --proxy-record
options.description: With --proxy: append each proxied response to this recording file (record-through capture).

options.name: --select
options.description: Disambiguator when the recording file contains multiple recordings.

options.name: --no-watch
options.description: Disable hot-reload on file changes. [default: False]

options.name: --stateful
options.description: Stateful cursor mode (each request advances). [default: False]

options.name: --stateful-once
options.description: Stateful + no wrap-around at the end of the recording. [default: False]

options.name: --loop
options.description: Loop proactive emitters indefinitely. [default: False]

options.name: --auto-install
options.description: Auto-install missing protocol plugins. [default: False]

options.name: --chaos
options.description: Chaos injection: e.g. "latency:100-500,fail-rate:0.05".

options.name: --faults
options.description: Per-method fault rules from a mock-faults.json sidecar (latency distributions, error rates, partial responses, connection drops).

options.name: --capture-miss
options.description: Persist unmatched requests to this file.

options.name: --control-token
options.description: Auth token for the runtime-scenario-switch control endpoint.

options.name: --mock-config
options.description: Path to a mock-configuration JSON (per-field response overrides refining a schema mock).

options.name: --require-auth
options.description: Require a bearer token equal to this value on every HTTP/WebSocket mocked request (401 otherwise). Plugin transports (MQTT/DIS/…) are not gated.

arguments.name: PATH
arguments.description: Path to a Bowire .bwr recording. Equivalent to --recording <path>; convenient for one-shot replay. See docs/recordings/bwr-format.md for the file format.

commands.name: mcp
commands.description: Expose Bowire as an MCP server for AI agents.

commands.name: serve
commands.description: Run Bowire as an MCP server (AI-agent bridge).

options.name: --bind
options.description: Transport for the MCP server. [default: stdio]

options.name: --port
options.description: Port for --bind http. [default: 5081]

options.name: --allow-arbitrary-urls
options.description: Drop the URL allowlist. Only safe in sandboxed contexts. [default: False]

options.name: --no-env-allowlist
options.description: Skip seeding the allowlist from ~/.bowire/environments.json. [default: False]

options.name: --allow-invoke
options.description: Widen the allowlist to every URL the user has typed at least once (~/.bowire/typed-urls.json). Strictly additive with the environments seed. [default: False]

options.name: --no-confirm
options.description: Skip the two-step pending-confirmation gate on mutator tools (bowire.mock.start, bowire.record.start). Use when the agent host already enforces approvals. [default: False]

options.name: --attach
options.description: Forwarder mode (#286): relay every incoming MCP request to a parent Bowire MCP endpoint. Accepts host:port shorthand (expanded to http://host:port/bowire/mcp) or an absolute http(s) URI. Mutually exclusive in spirit with --allow-arbitrary-urls / --allow-invoke / --no-confirm — those configure the *local* tool registry, which forwarder mode skips entirely.

options.name: --attach-token
options.description: Bearer token attached to every outbound request to the parent (Authorization: Bearer <token>). Required when the parent was started with --token <secret>.

options.name: --token
options.description: Require Authorization: Bearer <secret> on every inbound /bowire/mcp request (--bind http only). Pair with --attach-token on the child.

commands.name: test
commands.description: Run an assertion-based test suite. Accepts a recording JSON (v2.1 test-collection format) or a Flow JSON document (v2.2 — the T2 CI runner). Format auto-detected.

options.name: --url
options.description: Override the recording's serverUrl.

options.name: --report
options.description: Write an HTML report to this path.

options.name: --junit
options.description: Write a JUnit XML report to this path.

options.name: --sarif
options.description: Write a SARIF 2.1.0 report to this path (GitHub Code Scanning, GitLab, Azure DevOps).

options.name: --annotations
options.description: Emit GitHub Actions ::error annotations for every failure (inline PR annotations without a reporter action). [default: False]

options.name: --update-snapshots
options.description: Re-capture every snapshot baseline from the actual responses instead of diffing (Flow files only). [default: False]

options.name: --fail-on
options.description: Exit-code threshold: 'any' (default — non-zero on any failed check) or 'never' (run + report but always exit 0; a step error still exits 2). [default: any]

options.name: --workspace
options.description: Run every Flow JSON under a git-native workspace directory (its flows/ folder, or the directory itself). Aggregates pass/fail across all flows; the positional file is ignored.

options.name: --base-url
options.description: Fallback server URL for Flow steps that don't set their own serverUrl. Flow JSON files only; ignored for recordings.

options.name: --env
options.description: Variable for the Flow {{name}} / ${name} resolver. KEY=VALUE; repeatable. --vars is an alias.

options.name: --env-file
options.description: File with one KEY=VALUE per line (dotenv-style; blank lines and # comments ignored) for the Flow resolver. Repeatable; --env repeats win over file entries. [default: System.String[]]

options.name: --keyring
options.description: Resolve {{keyring.service/account}} refs from the runner's OS credential store (Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / libsecret) instead of an --env-file, so CI secrets never touch the flow file. Requires the Kuestenlogik.Bowire.Keyring package (bundled in the CLI). Flow files only. Maps to Bowire:Test:Keyring. [default: False]

options.name: --ai-seed
options.description: Deterministic seed for {{ai.*}} refs. In the workbench ai refs resolve via a model; the CLI has none, so a seed pins each ref to a stable value derived from the seed + ref name (no model call), making CI runs byte-reproducible. Unset leaves ai refs unresolved. Flow files only. Maps to Bowire:Test:AiSeed.

arguments.name: FILE
arguments.description: Path to a recording (v2.1) or Flow JSON file (v2.2). Format is auto-detected by JSON shape.

commands.name: import
commands.description: Convert external trace formats into Bowire recordings.

commands.name: har
commands.description: Convert a HAR 1.2 document into a .bwr recording.

options.name: --out
options.description: Output path for the recording. Use "-" to stream to stdout. Default: <har-basename>.bwr next to the input file.

options.name: --name
options.description: Recording name. Defaults to the HAR creator name or "Imported HAR".

options.name: --redact-secrets
options.description: Strip credential-bearing header values (Authorization, Cookie, X-Api-Key, …) before writing the recording — so a HAR captured against production never persists live tokens / session cookies. Detected credential headers are reported either way. [default: False]

arguments.name: FILE
arguments.description: Path to the HAR document.

commands.name: jwt
commands.description: JWT decode / tamper toolkit. Tier-2 anchor of the security-testing lane (see docs/architecture/security-testing.md).

commands.name: decode
commands.description: Decode a JWT and pretty-print the header + payload.

arguments.name: TOKEN
arguments.description: The JWT to operate on (header.payload.signature).

commands.name: analyze
commands.description: Deterministic JWT security analysis — flags alg=none, symmetric HMAC, missing/expired/long-lived exp, missing nbf, scope creep, audience binding, kid surface.

options.name: --audience
options.description: Expected audience — cross-checked against the token's aud claim.

arguments.name: TOKEN
arguments.description: The JWT to operate on (header.payload.signature).

commands.name: tamper
commands.description: Produce a tampered JWT (alg:none downgrade, claim mutation, optional HS256 re-signing).

options.name: --alg-none
options.description: Downgrade the token to alg:none (drops the signature; the classic JWT bypass). [default: False]

options.name: --set
options.description: Mutate a payload claim: --set claim=value. Repeatable. Values parsed as JSON literals first (so --set exp=9999999999 lands as number) and fall back to string.

options.name: --secret
options.description: Re-sign with HMAC-SHA256 using this secret (overrides --alg-none). Useful when probing weak-secret-based JWT validation.

arguments.name: TOKEN
arguments.description: The JWT to operate on (header.payload.signature).

commands.name: fuzz
commands.description: Schema-aware fuzzing of a single field. Tier-2 anchor of the security-testing lane.

options.name: --target
options.description: Target base URL.

options.name: --template
options.description: Recording-style JSON file describing the request shape (httpVerb / httpPath / body).

options.name: --field
options.description: JSONPath into the request body identifying the field to fuzz (e.g. $.username or $.filter.id).

options.name: --payloads
options.description: Payload category: sqli / xss / pathtrav / cmdinj.

options.name: --force
options.description: Run even when the field's value-shape doesn't match the payload class (e.g. fuzz a numeric field with string payloads anyway). [default: False]

options.name: --timeout
options.description: Per-payload HTTP timeout in seconds. Default 30.

options.name: --allow-self-signed-certs
options.description: Accept self-signed certs on the target. [default: False]

options.name: --auth-header
options.description: Add an HTTP header to every fuzz request (typically Authorization: Bearer …). Repeatable.

commands.name: proxy
commands.description: Intercepting HTTP/HTTPS proxy. Tier-3 anchor of the security-testing lane (see docs/architecture/security-testing.md).

options.name: --port
options.description: Port the proxy listens on (point browser / client at it). Default 8888.

options.name: --api-port
options.description: Sidecar API port the workbench's Proxy tab reads captured flows from. Default 8889.

options.name: --capacity
options.description: Maximum number of flows retained in memory (FIFO eviction). Default 1000.

options.name: --no-mitm
options.description: Disable HTTPS interception — CONNECT requests are tunneled-and-rejected with 501. Default: MITM enabled. [default: False]

options.name: --ca-dir
options.description: Override the CA storage directory. Default: ~/.bowire (PFX + DER cert persisted there).

options.name: --export-ca
options.description: Copy the public CA certificate to this path (.crt) and exit. Install the file into your trust store to suppress client-side warnings during HTTPS interception.

commands.name: interceptor
commands.description: Standalone reverse-proxy mode (#307 — Phase C of #153). Fronts an upstream service: clients point at Bowire's listener, every request is forwarded upstream and captured into the same InterceptedFlowStore the embedded middleware (UseBowireInterceptor) uses. The workbench's 'Intercepted' rail reads the sidecar API surface this command exposes.

options.name: --upstream
options.description: Upstream service URL the listener forwards to (e.g. https://api.example.com). Required.

options.name: --listen
options.description: host:port the edge listener binds to (e.g. 127.0.0.1:8080, 0.0.0.0:9000, :8080). Default 127.0.0.1:0 (loopback + ephemeral port).

options.name: --api-port
options.description: Sidecar API port the workbench's Intercepted rail reads from. Default 5089.

options.name: --capacity
options.description: Maximum number of flows retained in memory (FIFO eviction). Default 1000.

options.name: --max-body-bytes
options.description: Per-side body capture cap. Default 1048576 (1 MiB).

options.name: --allow-self-signed-upstream
options.description: Accept the upstream's TLS cert without chain validation. Useful when fronting a dev-mode service with a self-signed cert. Off by default. [default: False]

options.name: --tls
options.description: Serve HTTPS on the edge listener using a leaf certificate minted from Bowire's MITM CA (reuses #36's CA flow). Install the CA into the client trust store via `bowire proxy --export-ca` to avoid handshake warnings. [default: False]

options.name: --tls-host
options.description: Hostname the minted leaf certificate is issued for (SAN). Default: the listen address. Set when clients connect via a custom DNS name (e.g. api.local pointing to 127.0.0.1).

options.name: --ca-dir
options.description: Override the CA storage directory (default: ~/.bowire). Same flag as `bowire proxy`.

options.description: Override the info.version field. Defaults to '1.0.0' or the first service.Version found.

arguments.name: URL
arguments.description: URL to run discovery against (http(s)://, mqtt://, nats://, kafka://, ws://, amqp://, ...).

commands.name: workspace
commands.description: Manage Bowire workspaces — init a git-backed workspace directory (#147 / #149), migrate a legacy bundle-shaped workspace to the per-entity file layout (#196 Phase 2.2), or export/import the workspace state as a single JSON file (#149).

commands.name: init
commands.description: Materialise a fresh git-backed workspace directory at the given path. Drops the canonical folder skeleton (environments / collections / recordings / scripts / flows / secrets), a workspace.json manifest, and a default .gitignore that excludes secrets + cache files. Runs `git init` unless --no-git is passed.

options.name: --name
options.description: Workspace display name written into workspace.json. Defaults to the directory's basename.

options.name: --color
options.description: Workspace accent color (hex like '#22c55e'). Defaults to '#6366f1'.

options.name: --no-git
options.description: Skip the trailing `git init`. Useful when initialising inside an existing repository. [default: False]

arguments.name: PATH
arguments.description: Directory to initialise. Created if it doesn't exist; required to be empty so the init never clobbers existing content.

commands.name: migrate-format
commands.description: Convert a workspace from the legacy bundle layout (one <entityKind>.json per kind) into the per-entity file layout the git-backed runtime reads through. Idempotent: re-running on an already-migrated workspace is a no-op. The original bundle files are renamed to .legacy so an operator can verify the per-entity files before deleting them.

arguments.name: PATH
arguments.description: Directory containing the workspace to migrate. Existing per-entity files are preserved; only legacy <entityKind>.json bundles are converted.

commands.name: export
commands.description: Read every entity from a per-entity workspace directory and write a single self-contained JSON file. Round-trips through 'workspace import' without touching ~/.bowire/. Useful for CI / scripted setup, archiving, or shipping a workspace snapshot.

options.name: --from
options.description: Workspace storage root to read from. When omitted, the current directory is used. The directory must contain at least one of the per-entity buckets (environments/, collections/, recordings/, scripts/, flows/).

arguments.name: PATH
arguments.description: Output file path. The exporter writes a single indented JSON document with workspaceFormatVersion + one array per entity kind.

commands.name: import
commands.description: Materialise a workspace export (the single-JSON shape 'workspace export' produces) into a target directory as the per-entity layout. Existing entries with the same id are overwritten; entries the export doesn't carry are left alone.

options.name: --to
options.description: Target workspace directory to write into. When omitted, the current directory is used. Created if missing.

arguments.name: PATH
arguments.description: Path to the .json export file produced by 'workspace export'.

commands.name: catalogue
commands.description: Inspect and select the URL/service catalogue the workbench browses (#136). 'list' prints the entries the active provider returns, 'providers' shows which provider implementations are installed, 'use' persists a provider override to ~/.bowire/catalogue-config.json (the same file the workbench's Settings → Catalogue providers tab writes), and 'clear' drops it again.

commands.name: list
commands.description: Fetch a catalogue and print its entries. With --provider (plus its --path / --url / --consul detail) it reads that provider without persisting anything; with no flags it reads whatever the workbench would — the persisted override from `catalogue use`, or nothing. Exits 1 when no provider is configured so a CI step can gate on it.

options.name: --provider
options.description: Provider id: local / http / consul / kubernetes / agent. kubernetes + agent require the matching Kuestenlogik.Bowire.Catalogue.* package (`bowire plugin install …`).

options.name: --path
options.description: Catalogue file for the 'local' provider. Defaults to ~/.bowire/catalogue.json.

options.name: --url
options.description: Catalogue document URL for the 'http' provider.

options.name: --consul
options.description: Consul agent address for the 'consul' provider (e.g. http://localhost:8500).

options.name: --json
options.description: Emit the raw snapshot as JSON ({ providerId, providerName, entries: [...] }) instead of the human table. [default: False]

commands.name: providers
commands.description: List the catalogue provider implementations loaded in this install. local / http / consul ship in the core package; kubernetes and agent only appear after `bowire plugin install Kuestenlogik.Bowire.Catalogue.Kubernetes` / `.Agent`.

options.name: --json
options.description: Emit [{ id, name }] as JSON. [default: False]

commands.name: use
commands.description: Persist a catalogue-provider override to ~/.bowire/catalogue-config.json. The workbench reads the same file on boot, so this is the scriptable equivalent of picking a provider in Settings → Catalogue providers. Overrides whatever appsettings.json configures until `catalogue clear` runs.

options.name: --path
options.description: Catalogue file for the 'local' provider. Defaults to ~/.bowire/catalogue.json.

options.name: --url
options.description: Catalogue document URL for the 'http' provider.

options.name: --consul
options.description: Consul agent address for the 'consul' provider (e.g. http://localhost:8500).

options.name: --token
options.description: Auth secret for the chosen provider — the Consul ACL token, or the HTTP provider's Authorization header value. Stored in plaintext in ~/.bowire/catalogue-config.json; prefer appsettings + a secret store on shared machines.

arguments.name: PROVIDER
arguments.description: Provider id to activate: local / http / consul / kubernetes / agent.

commands.name: clear
commands.description: Delete the persisted catalogue override (~/.bowire/catalogue-config.json) so the host falls back to Bowire:Discovery:Catalogue in appsettings.json (or to no catalogue at all).

commands.name: recording
commands.description: Standalone tooling for .bwr files — workspace-agnostic. Exposes `validate` and `correlate`; `info` / `diff` / `extract` slot in here when needed.

commands.name: validate
commands.description: Parse + schema-check a .bwr file. Verifies recordingFormatVersion is supported by this build, at least one step is present, and no step carries a responseRef body-ref (a standalone .bwr inlines every body). Exit 0 on success, 64 bad args, 65 malformed file, 66 file not found.

options.name: --name
options.description: Disambiguate when the file is a store-wrapped envelope with multiple recordings. Matches against the recording's `name` or `id` field.

arguments.name: PATH
arguments.description: Path to the .bwr file to validate.

commands.name: correlate
commands.description: Read a .bwr as one correlated transaction: resolve a correlation signal (a traceparent / x-correlation-id header, else a shared id-shaped payload field), then print every step on a shared time axis with a strong/weak/derived/no-match verdict. A step the key misses is still joined when it shares a distinctive id-shaped value with a step the key matched, and the `via` column names that value. Exit 0 on success, 64 bad args, 65 malformed file, 66 file not found.

options.name: --name
options.description: Disambiguate when the file is a store-wrapped envelope with multiple recordings. Matches against the recording's `name` or `id` field.

options.name: --key
options.description: Correlate on this key instead of the auto-detected one, as `name=value` (e.g. `--key shipId=101`). Overrides any `correlation` field persisted in the file.

options.name: --json
options.description: Emit the full correlation model as JSON instead of the table — the same shape the workbench's /api/recordings/correlate returns. [default: False]

arguments.name: PATH
arguments.description: Path to the .bwr file to correlate.

commands.name: contract
commands.description: Pact-style consumer contract testing. `publish` builds a contract from a recording (+ optional broker push); `verify` replays it against a live provider.

commands.name: publish
commands.description: Build a consumer contract from a recording and write it to a file (and, with --broker-url, push it to a Pact Broker).

options.name: --provider
options.description: Provider name the contract is against (required).

options.name: --consumer
options.description: Consumer name. Defaults to the recording's name.

options.name: --out
options.description: Output contract file path. Defaults to <consumer>-<provider>.pact.json.

options.name: --broker-url
options.description: Pact Broker base URL to PUT the contract to (outbound — opt-in). Omit to only write the file.

options.name: --consumer-version
options.description: Consumer version for the broker publish. Defaults to a timestamp.

options.name: --tag
options.description: Tag the published consumer version on the broker (e.g. a branch name).

arguments.name: RECORDING
arguments.description: Path to a recording / .bwr file captured on the consumer side.

commands.name: verify
commands.description: Replay a consumer contract against a live provider and fail on any mismatch. Exit 0 = all held, 1 = a mismatch, 2 = a request errored.

options.name: --provider-url
options.description: Base URL of the live provider to replay against (required).

options.name: --broker-url
options.description: Pact Broker base URL to pull the latest contract from (outbound — opt-in). Requires --provider.

options.name: --provider
options.description: Provider name to pull from the broker (with --broker-url).

options.name: --tag
options.description: Pull the latest contract carrying this tag (with --broker-url).

options.name: --junit
options.description: Write a JUnit XML report to this path.

options.name: --sarif
options.description: Write a SARIF 2.1.0 report to this path.

arguments.name: CONTRACT
arguments.description: Path to a contract file. Omit and use --broker-url + --provider to pull the latest from a broker.

commands.name: auth-recording
commands.description: Manage captured auth recordings — the credentials a mock's auth requirement resolves by id. capture / list / remove; the same store the workbench picker and the MCP tools use.

commands.name: capture
commands.description: Store a credential as a named auth recording — statically from --credential-env, or by running an auth flow with --flow. Exit 0 ok, 64 bad args, 65 store/flow error, 66 flow file not found.

options.name: --id
options.description: Recording id, referenced by a mock's auth.authRecordingId.

options.name: --credential-env
options.description: Static capture: name of the environment variable holding the credential to store. Read from the environment so the secret never lands in shell history or process args.

options.name: --flow
options.description: Flow capture: path to an auth-flow definition JSON (a scriptable login → token chain). Bowire RUNS it (outbound HTTP) and stores the captured token. Secrets in the flow come from {{env.NAME}}. Mutually exclusive with --credential-env.

options.name: --name
options.description: Human label shown in the picker (default: the id).

options.name: --scheme
options.description: Credential scheme for static capture: bearer / basic / apikey (flow capture derives it from the flow). [default: bearer]

options.name: --header
options.description: Header the credential is presented in (default: Authorization).

options.name: --workspace
options.description: Workspace to scope the recording to (default: the shared, unscoped store).

commands.name: list
commands.description: List captured auth recordings — credential-free (ids, names, schemes).

options.name: --workspace
options.description: Workspace to scope the recording to (default: the shared, unscoped store).

commands.name: remove
commands.description: Delete a captured auth recording.

options.name: --workspace
options.description: Workspace to scope the recording to (default: the shared, unscoped store).

arguments.name: ID
arguments.description: Recording id to remove.

commands.name: version
commands.description: Print the Bowire version and runtime; with --plugins, also the loaded protocol plugins and their versions.

options.name: --plugins
options.description: Also list the loaded protocol plugins and their versions. [default: False]

commands.name: scan
commands.description: Run vulnerability templates against a target URL. The Tier-1 anchor of the security-testing lane (see docs/architecture/security-testing.md).

options.name: --target
options.description: Target base URL (e.g. https://api.example.com).

options.name: --templates
options.description: Directory of *.json vulnerability templates to run (Bowire format).

options.name: --template
options.description: Single template *.json file to run (combinable with --templates).

options.name: --nuclei
options.description: Directory of *.yaml Nuclei templates (projectdiscovery/nuclei-templates). Read alongside --templates; resolved against --target so {{BaseURL}}/{{Hostname}} etc. land on real probes.

options.name: --cve-db
options.description: Path to a CVE / VulnDb JSON file for the banner CVE-lookup (Server / X-Powered-By version → known CVEs). Runs with the built-in passive checks; defaults to a small built-in seed when omitted.

options.name: --oast-server
options.description: URL of an interactsh-compatible interaction server for out-of-band detection, e.g. https://oast.example.com. Enables templates that prove a BLIND finding (SSRF / RCE / XXE) by planting a callback host and checking whether the target contacted it — the response itself shows nothing. Points at any instance: your own (`bowire oast serve` / interactsh-server) or a third party's. OFF by default: without it the scanner makes no outbound call beyond the target, and out-of-band templates are skipped rather than reported as clean.

options.name: --oast-wait
options.description: Seconds to wait after the probes before polling for callbacks. A target's DNS lookup / fetch arrives asynchronously, so polling immediately would miss it and call the target clean. Default 5.

options.name: --oast-token
options.description: Auth token for a gated interaction server (one started with `bowire oast serve --token`). Sent verbatim as the Authorization header. Omit for an open instance.

options.name: --auth-flow
options.description: Path to a headless auth-flow JSON file (login → token chain). Runs once before the scan; the captured token is injected as an auth header into every probe (refresh on expiry). Secrets are read from {{env.NAME}}, never inlined. Covers scriptable grants (client-credentials, password, refresh) — browser grants (OAuth auth-code/device) are not yet supported.

options.name: --out
options.description: Write findings as SARIF 2.1.0 JSON to this path (for CI dashboards: GitHub Code Scanning, GitLab, Azure DevOps).

options.name: --suite
options.description: Run a named suite after the scan. `owasp-api` = OWASP API Top 10 rollup (HTTP + protocol probes) with a per-entry coverage table; `protocol` = only the protocol-specific probes (gRPC/GraphQL/WS/MQTT/SSE/MCP) + the table — use for non-HTTP targets like mqtt:// or ws://; `all` = everything (HTTP OWASP + protocol probes) + the table.

options.name: --severity
options.description: Minimum severity to report: low / medium / high / critical. Lower-severity templates still load but are reported as skipped.

options.name: --timeout
options.description: Per-probe HTTP timeout in seconds. Default 30.

options.name: --dns-resolver
options.description: Nameserver IP for Nuclei `dns:` templates, e.g. 1.1.1.1. Defaults to the machine's resolvers. Worth setting deliberately: a split-horizon or filtering resolver answers differently from the public view a subdomain-takeover template assumes, and the wrong answer reads as 'not vulnerable' rather than as an error.

options.name: --allow-code-templates
options.description: Run Nuclei `code:` templates. OFF by default, and think before turning it on: a code: template is a PROGRAM that executes on this machine with your rights, not a request sent to the target, and the nuclei-templates corpus is community-supplied. Bowire runs it in a child process with an interpreter allow-list, a wall-clock kill and an output cap — that bounds a hang or a crash, it is not a sandbox. Without the flag such templates load and report as skipped. `javascript:` templates never run: they need Nuclei's own embedded JS runtime. [default: False]

options.name: --code-template-interpreters
options.description: Interpreters `code:` templates may be launched with, e.g. `deno bun`. REPLACES the default set (sh, bash, zsh, py, python, python3, node, ruby, perl, pwsh, powershell) rather than adding to it, so it narrows as readily as it widens — pass `python3` alone to permit nothing else. Needs --allow-code-templates; on its own it changes nothing, because nothing runs.

options.name: --allow-self-signed-certs
options.description: Accept self-signed / untrusted TLS certs on the target. Off by default — use only when probing a known dev/staging cert. [default: False]

options.name: --no-builtins
options.description: Skip the built-in passive checks (TLS-version enumeration, version-disclosing headers, verbose-error detection). Built-ins run by default. [default: False]

options.name: --scope
options.description: In-scope hostname or glob (e.g. `api.example.com` or `*.example.com` — the leading `*.` matches sub-domains but NOT the apex). Repeat or comma-separate. Defaults to the target's own host, so accidental cross-host probes are blocked unless explicitly widened.

options.name: --auth-header
options.description: Add an HTTP header to every probe — typically `Authorization: Bearer <token>` or `X-Api-Key: <key>`. Repeatable for multiple headers (cookies, multi-header auth schemes). Without this flag, scans of authenticated APIs land on the login wall and the scanner reports misleading 'endpoint missing' findings.

options.name: --auth-header-b
options.description: A SECOND identity's auth header(s), same shape as --auth-header. Enables the OWASP API1 BOLA check: the object at --target is read as identity A (--auth-header) and then as identity B; if B can read A's object while anonymous access is blocked, object-level authorization is missing. Repeatable.

options.name: --active
options.description: Enable the ACTIVE (mutating / aggressive) probe tier (#395–#400) — OFF by default. Active probes may PUBLISH to the target (MQTT retained-message poisoning), hold connections open, or open many streams. Each namespaces + cleans up its side effects, but this deliberately mutates the target: use only against systems you are authorised to test. [default: False]

options.name: --active-duration
options.description: Wall-clock budget in seconds for time-based active probes (slow-loris / slow-consumption). Default 15.

options.name: --active-concurrency
options.description: Concurrency budget (N) for fan-out active probes (gRPC concurrent-stream). The verdict is honest about the number reached. Default 100.

options.name: --active-expected-topic
options.description: Expected-topic scope for the MQTT wildcard-subscribe active probe (#396) — the topics an authenticated client is meant to reach. Delivered traffic outside this set is flagged. Repeatable / comma-separated.

commands.name: spider
commands.description: Discover candidate endpoints from a base URL (robots.txt, sitemap.xml, an OpenAPI/Swagger document, a common-path HEAD sweep, and same-origin page links). Conservative: same-host/--scope only, honours robots.txt, never authenticates beyond --auth-header.

options.name: --url
options.description: Base URL to crawl (e.g. https://api.example.com).

options.name: --scope
options.description: In-scope hostname or `*.`-glob. Repeat / comma-separate. Defaults to the base URL's host.

options.name: --auth-header
options.description: Header applied to every request, e.g. `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. Repeatable.

options.name: --timeout
options.description: Per-request HTTP timeout in seconds. Default 30.

options.name: --no-robots
options.description: Ignore robots.txt Disallow rules (default: respected). [default: False]

options.name: --max
options.description: Maximum candidates to collect. Default 500.

options.name: --allow-self-signed-certs
options.description: Accept self-signed / untrusted TLS on the target. [default: False]

options.name: --out
options.description: Write the candidate list as JSON to this path.

commands.name: mutate
commands.description: Print the schema-aware mutations (targeted invalid inputs) the engine produces for a field type — type-confusion, boundary, encoding, enum-bypass, structural. Seeded + budgeted for reproducibility.

options.name: --type
options.description: Field type: integer / number / string / boolean / enum / array / object.

options.name: --enum
options.description: Comma-separated allowed values (for --type enum) — adds a case-variant-bypass mutation.

options.name: --required
options.description: Treat the field as required — adds an omitted/null violation. [default: False]

options.name: --format
options.description: Format hint (email / uuid / date / uri / ipv4) — adds a format-violation mutation.

options.name: --seed
options.description: Seed for reproducible mutation selection under a budget. Default 0.

options.name: --budget
options.description: Max mutations to emit for the field (0 = all). Keeps scans bounded.

commands.name: report
commands.description: Turn a scan SARIF artifact (bowire scan --out) into a markdown report — findings grouped by severity + OWASP, optionally diffed vs a baseline SARIF. Deterministic; the AI executive-summary layer is POST /api/ai/security-report.

options.name: --in
options.description: SARIF file to report on (from `bowire scan --out`).

options.name: --baseline
options.description: A previous run's SARIF to diff against — the report adds new / fixed / still-open sections.

options.name: --out
options.description: Write the markdown report to this path (default: print to stdout).

options.name: --target
options.description: Target name to title the report with (e.g. api.example.com).

commands.name: vulndb
commands.description: Manage the local vulnerability-template cache (~/.bowire/vulndb) that `bowire scan` reads by default. See docs/architecture/security-testing.md.

commands.name: update
commands.description: Fetch / refresh the curated Bowire.VulnDb template set into ~/.bowire/vulndb. With no --source this pulls the latest GitHub release (the only outbound call, and only because you asked). Point --source at a repo checkout, a .tar.gz, or a URL for air-gapped / pinned installs.

options.name: --source
options.description: Template source: a directory (repo checkout / mirror), a .tar.gz file, or an http(s) URL to a tarball. Omit to fetch the latest Kuestenlogik/Bowire.VulnDb GitHub release.

options.name: --dest
options.description: Cache directory to write into. Default: ~/.bowire/vulndb.

options.name: --ref
options.description: Release tag to pin when fetching from GitHub (e.g. v0.1.0). Ignored for --source directory/file/URL. Default: the latest release.

commands.name: list
commands.description: List the templates in the local cache (~/.bowire/vulndb) — protocol, severity, id, and name, plus a total. Reads the templates-index.json sidecar when present, else walks the tree.

options.name: --dest
options.description: Cache directory to read. Default: ~/.bowire/vulndb.

options.name: --protocol
options.description: Only list templates under this protocol folder (grpc / graphql / rest / odata / …).

commands.name: monitor
commands.description: Passive monitoring — run saved recordings as scheduled health probes, record every outcome, and alert on pass↔fail transitions (Postman Monitors / AWS Synthetics analog).

commands.name: run
commands.description: Load probe file(s) and run them on their schedule, writing every outcome to the ledger and signalling on transitions. Ctrl+C stops.

options.name: --ledger-root
options.description: Directory for the append-only outcome ledgers. Default ~/.bowire/monitoring.

options.name: --once
options.description: Run each probe exactly once and exit instead of looping — for CI / smoke tests. Exit code 2 when any probe fails or errors. [default: False]

options.name: --signal
options.description: Outbound alert channel as '<scheme>:<arg>' — e.g. 'slack:https://hooks.slack.com/...' or 'pagerduty:<routing-key>'. Repeatable. Each scheme is served by an opt-in signaler package; an unknown scheme is reported and skipped. The console channel is always on.

arguments.name: PROBE_FILES
arguments.description: One or more probe definition files (JSON: { name, schedule, severity, assertions, recording }).

commands.name: oast
commands.description: Out-of-band interaction server (OAST) — the callback catcher that proves blind SSRF / RCE / XXE. See docs/architecture/security-testing.md.

commands.name: serve
commands.description: Run the interaction server: a DNS + HTTP catcher for *.<domain> plus the register/poll API. Wire-compatible with interactsh, so `bowire scan --oast-server` (or any interactsh client) can point at it. Requires the domain to be NS-delegated to this host — see docs/architecture/security-testing.md.

options.name: --domain
options.description: The delegated zone this instance is authoritative for, e.g. oast.example.com. Callback hosts are handed out beneath it. The zone must be NS-delegated to this host or nothing will ever reach the DNS catcher.

options.name: --public-ip
options.description: This host's public IP. Answered for A queries under --domain, so a target that resolves a callback host and then connects also lands on the HTTP catcher (upgrading the evidence from 'looked it up' to 'actually connected').

options.name: --http-port
options.description: HTTP catcher + API port. Default 80.

options.name: --dns-port
options.description: DNS catcher port. Default 53. A real delegation cannot use another port — override only for local testing.

options.name: --listen-ip
options.description: Address to bind. Default 0.0.0.0 (all interfaces).

options.name: --token
options.description: Require this value as the Authorization header on /register. Without it the instance is an OPEN callback catcher: anyone who finds it can register and point it at third-party targets.

options.name: --session-idle-minutes
options.description: Evict sessions that stop polling after this long. Default 60. Keeps a long-lived catcher from holding other people's callback traffic indefinitely.
